Alphabet in “Stijl letters”

Van Doesburg’s capital alphabet of about 1919, built only from thick horizontal and vertical strokes on a square module.

Source
Wikimedia Commons: Theo van Doesburg, Alphabet
Creator
Theo van Doesburg
Made
About 1919 (Commons, after the Hoek catalogue; the 1968 exhibition dated the photograph 1918–1919)
Style
De Stijl (agent-proposed, not yet reviewed by a person)
Moods
Rectilinear, heavy, systematic
Evidence
Inspected the Commons image (3774 × 579 px, viewed at 1920 px), scanned from Joost Baljeu, Theo van Doesburg (1974), pp. 108–109. The object is a photograph of the alphabet, 3.5 × 17 cm, in the Centraal Museum Utrecht on loan from the Dutch State (RCE inventory AB5936).
Reviewed
28 September 2026
Rights
Open license, stored. License: public domain. Rights policy

Context

Commons describes the object as “Alfabet in ‘Stijlletters’”, a photograph made in Leiden, inherited by Nelly van Doesburg in 1931 and given to the Dutch State by Wies van Moorsel in 1981. Commons.

The Foundry’s digital typeface Architype Van Doesburg revives the alphabet.

Observed

  • Twenty-six capitals, A to M in the top row and N to Z in the bottom row, in solid black on white.
  • Every stroke is horizontal or vertical and of the same thickness; there are no curves or diagonals.
  • Letters that normally need diagonals, such as K, M, N, V, W, X, Y, and Z, are rebuilt from right-angled steps.
  • Counters are small rectangles; the letters are nearly square and set with narrow gaps.
  • Faint text from the facing book page shows through at the right.

Why it belongs

The alphabet applies the painting rule to type: no curves and no diagonals. Legibility suffers for letters such as K, X, and Z, which is the known cost of the approach.

The same letterforms appear in van Doesburg’s poster design for La Section d’Or.

Borrow

Build display capitals from one stroke weight on a square grid, and replace diagonals with right-angled steps.

Keep such letters for short words; use a plain sans-serif for running text.
